In the electrolysis, $\text{O}^{2-}$ donates electrons at the anode and produces $\text{O}_2$ gas. $\text{Al}^{3+}$ present in the solution accepts the electron at the cathode and turns into $\text{Al}$ metal.

$$6\text{O}^{2-} \longrightarrow 3\text{O}_2 + 12\text{e}^- \quad \text{(Anode reaction)}$$
$$2\text{Al}^{3+} + 6\text{e}^- \longrightarrow 2\text{Al} \quad \text{(Cathode reaction)}$$

Metal is extracted by heating carbon along with metallic oxide. For example, $\text{Zn}$ from $\text{ZnO}$, $\text{Fe}$ from $\text{FeO}$, $\text{Pb}$ from $\text{PbO}$, or $\text{Cu}$ from $\text{CuO}$ are extracted this way.

$$\text{ZnO} + \text{C} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Zn} + \text{CO}$$
$$\text{FeO} + \text{C} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Fe} + \text{CO}$$
$$\text{PbO} + \text{C} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Pb} + \text{CO}$$
$$\text{CuO} + \text{C} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Cu} + \text{CO}$$

This method is called carbon reduction. The mid level position holder metals in the reactivity series are extracted in this method.
